summary: A 1950 New Jersey Forest Fire Service tower of 80 feet in Brendan Byrne State Forest, built to replace an earlier Four Mile tripod and still listed as in active service.

facts.design: 80-foot Aermotor tower with a 7x7-foot metal cab, painted red and white

access.note: Owned, manned and maintained by the NJFFS as a working observation post; no source read describes public access to the cab.

events.note: NJFFS erected the Four Mile Tower, a wooden tripod; Wikipedia says the Lebanon Station replaced it (no replacement year given)
Built 1950 per the NHLR register page

evidence.supports: 80-foot Aermotor tower with 7x7 metal cab; replaced the old Four Mile tower
evidence.quote: The NJFFS 80’ Aermotor tower with 7’x7’ metal cab replaced the old Four Mile tower overlooking the fire-prone “pinelands.”

evidence.supports: Four Mile wooden tripod erected 1910, replaced by the Lebanon Station
evidence.quote: The New Jersey Forest Fire Service erected the "Four Mile Tower", a simple tripod of wooden poles, in 1910. It was replaced by the Lebanon Station.

evidence.supports: 80 feet (24 m) height; Division B; Brendan Byrne State Forest
evidence.quote: Lebanon Station 136 feet (41 m) 80 feet (24 m) Div. B Sec. B3, B6,(B5, B2) Brendan T. Byrne State Forest

evidence.supports: 54 years old at registration and among the state's oldest
evidence.quote: At 54 years, Lebanon Station fire tower is one of New Jersey’s oldest.

evidence.supports: owned, manned and maintained by NJFFS, Division B
evidence.quote: Tower owned, manned and maintained by New Jersey Forest Fire Service. Located in Division B jurisdiction.

evidence.supports: pine plantation grew to about 80 feet and blocked the view; harvest restored the vista and supplied lumber; no date
evidence.quote: In recent years a CCC era pine plantation grew to 80’ tall, restricting the view. A timely timber harvest restored the vista and supplied lumber for a variety of state projects.
Fresh painted in red and white NJFFS scheme.

evidence.supports: all NJFFS towers still in active service
evidence.quote: All towers are still in active service.

evidence.supports: Lebanon tower's location in Brendan Byrne State Forest, Burlington County, on the Division B list
evidence.quote: Brendan Byrne State Forest, Burlington County, New Jersey

evidence.supports: Lakewood tower decommissioned July 2024 on the same Division B page that says all towers are in active service
visit report dated January 12, 2007 (fresh red and white paint)
staffed at the 2007 visit report; usually manned year round
evidence.quote: Usually year round except during periods of wetness and snow cover.

sources.title: List of New Jersey Forest Fire Service fire towers

notes_for_editor: The 1950 build year and the register details rest on the NHLR page alone; no NJFFS, newspaper or state document was found for them. The register's visit-report staffing entry (staffed = yes) dates from January 12, 2007, so the staffing as_of is 2007; current staffing is not verified because the Division B page is undated. The Division B page says all towers are in active service yet also lists the Lakewood tower as decommissioned on July 3, 2024, so the story reports that claim with the caveat. No source found names the NJFFS as the builder, so the story says only that the register dates the tower to 1950. The site of the Four Mile tripod and the year it was replaced are unknown. The record's 24.0 m height matches Wikipedia's 80 ft (24 m). No new photos added; the existing NHLR photo is kept.
